page.layout: One printed page. Running head at the top, with page number 37 at the top right. Below it: one column of italic verse, then the author's initials "I. I. B." at the right. A rule, then a centred title "IN OBITVM PRINCIPIS" with subtitle "CONDÆI 1588.", then a poem with a large initial. Signature "C. ij." at the right foot. No margin notes.

main_text.l: Quem non perpetuis potuerunt perdere bellis
Quem nulla hostilis vicit victoria fortem

page.notes: The large initial at the start of the poem is a B with a following Cr[?] that I could not read with certainty; the first word is marked as doubtful. "Camœnæ" and "quænis" are doubtful readings. The first verse stanza is set in italic and has no stanza breaks in the scan; its lines run together as one paragraph. Long s is written as s throughout, and printed "vsque" is given as "usque".
